rows.stem:
Identify the product ‘X’ obtained in the following chemical reaction :

\(\mathrm{CaCO_3}\) \(\xrightarrow{\Delta}\) ‘X’ + \(\mathrm{CO_2}\)
rows.solution:
On heating, calcium carbonate (limestone) decomposes into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide:

\(\mathrm{CaCO_3(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} CaO(s) + CO_2(g)}\)

Calcium oxide is called quick lime. (Limestone is the reactant itself; gypsum and Plaster of Paris are calcium sulphates.)

This is option (A) Quick lime.

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem: Select a pair of natural indicator from the following :
rows.solution:
Litmus is a natural indicator extracted from lichen, and turmeric is a natural indicator from a plant. Methyl orange and phenolphthalein are synthetic indicators, so every other pair contains at least one synthetic indicator.

This is option (B) Turmeric and Litmus.

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem: A chemical compound used in glass, soap and paper industries is
rows.solution:
Washing soda (sodium carbonate, \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\)) is used in the glass, soap and paper industries. It is also used to make borax, as a domestic cleaning agent and to remove permanent hardness of water.

This is option (A) Washing Soda.

rows.stem: The structural formula of Cyclohexane is

options.label: A
options.text: Diagram (A) as printed - a six-membered carbon ring structural formula; see the attached figure.

options.label: B
options.text: Diagram (B) as printed - a six-membered carbon ring structural formula; see the attached figure.

options.label: C
options.text: Diagram (C) as printed - a six-membered carbon ring structural formula; see the attached figure.

options.label: D
options.text: Diagram (D) as printed - a six-membered carbon ring structural formula; see the attached figure.

rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - all four options are drawn six-membered carbon-ring structural formulas that differ only in their bonding and hydrogen count; the options ARE the figure. Described, not named, since naming them would state the answer. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
Cyclohexane, \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}}\), is a saturated ring: six carbon atoms joined to each other only by single bonds, with every carbon carrying two hydrogen atoms. Of the four drawings, only the one in which each ring carbon has two hydrogens and no double or triple bond appears shows this. The other three contain double or triple bonds, so they are unsaturated.

This is option (B).

rows.stem:
Consider the following Chemical equation :

a \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) + b \(\mathrm{HCl}\) \(\longrightarrow\) c \(\mathrm{AlCl_3}\) + d \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)

In order to balance this chemical equation, the values of a, b, c and d must be
rows.solution:
Balance aluminium first: 1 \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) gives 2 \(\mathrm{AlCl_3}\). That needs 6 Cl, so 6 HCl. The 3 O of \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) and the 6 H of 6 HCl make 3 \(\mathrm{H_2O}\):

\(\mathrm{Al_2O_3 + 6HCl \rightarrow 2AlCl_3 + 3H_2O}\)

Check: Al 2 = 2; O 3 = 3; H 6 = 6; Cl 6 = 6.

So a, b, c, d are 1, 6, 2, 3, which is option (A) 1, 6, 2 and 3.

rows.stem: Which one of the following hydrocarbons is different from the others ?
rows.solution:
\(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}\), \(\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}\) and \(\mathrm{C_2H_6}\) all fit \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}\), the general formula of the alkanes (saturated). \(\mathrm{C_7H_{14}}\) fits \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}}\), so it is an alkene (unsaturated).

This is option (B) \(\mathrm{C_7H_{14}}\).

rows.stem: Which one of the following reactions is different from the remaining three ?
rows.solution:
In three of the reactions two compounds exchange ions (double displacement), for example silver chloride is precipitated when sodium chloride reacts with silver nitrate. The reaction of calcium oxide with water forms a single product, calcium hydroxide, so it is a combination reaction.

This is option (B) \(\mathrm{CaO + H_2O \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2}\).

rows.stem: Select from the following a plant hormone which promotes cell division.
rows.solution:
Cytokinins promote cell division and are present in greater concentration where cell division is rapid, as in fruits and seeds. (Auxins and gibberellins promote growth by cell elongation, and abscisic acid inhibits growth.)

This is option (D) Cytokinins.

rows.stem: Part(s) of a flower which attracts insects for pollination is (are)
rows.solution:
The petals are brightly coloured and often scented, and they attract insects that carry out pollination. The sepals are usually green and protect the flower in the bud, while the anther and stigma are the reproductive parts.

This is option (C) petals only.

rows.stem: In an experiment to study independent inheritance of two separate traits : shape and colour of seeds, the ratio of the different combinations in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) progeny would be
rows.solution:
When two separate traits, seed shape (round or wrinkled) and seed colour (yellow or green), are followed together, the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation shows four combinations: round yellow, round green, wrinkled yellow and wrinkled green in the ratio 9 : 3 : 3 : 1. The new combinations show that the traits are inherited independently.

This is option (C) 9 : 3 : 3 : 1.

rows.stem:
Which of the following statement (s) is (are) true about human heart ?

(a) Right atrium receives oxygenated blood from lungs through pulmonary artery.

(b) Left atrium transfers oxygenated blood to left ventricle which sends it to various parts of the body.

(c) Right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from different parts of the body through vena cava.

(d) Left atrium transfers oxygenated blood to aorta which sends it to different parts of the body.
rows.solution:
Statement (a) is false: the right atrium receives deoxygenated blood, and oxygenated blood from the lungs comes to the left atrium through the pulmonary vein. Statement (b) is true. Statement (c) is true: deoxygenated blood from the body enters the right atrium through the vena cava. Statement (d) is false: it is the left ventricle, not the left atrium, that pumps blood into the aorta.

So statements (b) and (c) are true, which is option (C).

rows.stem: A cross between two tall pea plants resulted in offsprings having a few dwarf plants. The gene-combination of the parental plants must be
rows.solution:
Some offspring are dwarf (tt), so each parent must carry the recessive allele t. Both parents are tall, so each must also carry T. Both parents are therefore Tt.

\(\mathrm{Tt \times Tt}\) gives TT : Tt : tt = 1 : 2 : 1, so about one plant in four is dwarf, a few of the offspring. (A cross of Tt with tt would make half the plants dwarf, and a cross with a TT parent would give no dwarf plants.)

This is option (A) Tt and Tt.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: The Phenomena of light involved in the formation of a rainbow in the sky are

options.label: B
options.text: Refraction, dispersion and total internal reflection

rows.solution:
A rainbow forms in tiny water droplets. Sunlight entering a droplet is refracted and dispersed into its colours, reflected internally at the back of the droplet, and refracted again as it leaves. (The reflection inside the droplet is internal reflection, not total internal reflection, and scattering plays no part.)

This is option (D) Dispersion, refraction and internal reflection.

rows.stem: In case of four wires of same material, the resistance will be minimum if the diameter and length of the wire respectively are
rows.solution:
For wires of the same material, \(R = \rho\dfrac{l}{A}\) and \(A = \dfrac{\pi d^2}{4}\), so \(R\) is proportional to \(\dfrac{l}{d^2}\). Write the original diameter as \(d\) and length as \(l\):

diameter \(\dfrac{d}{2}\), length \(\dfrac{l}{4}\): \(\dfrac{l/4}{d^2/4} = \dfrac{l}{d^2}\)

diameter \(\dfrac{d}{4}\), length \(4l\): \(\dfrac{4l}{d^2/16} = \dfrac{64l}{d^2}\)

diameter \(2d\), length \(l\): \(\dfrac{l}{4d^2} = \dfrac{0{\cdot}25\,l}{d^2}\)

diameter \(4d\), length \(2l\): \(\dfrac{2l}{16d^2} = \dfrac{0{\cdot}125\,l}{d^2}\)

The last is the smallest, so that wire has the minimum resistance. This is option (D) 4D and 2L.

rows.stem: A food chain will be more advantageous in terms of energy if it has
rows.solution:
Only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level passes on to the next; the rest is lost at each step. The fewer the trophic levels, the more of the energy captured by the producers reaches the last consumer, so a food chain with 2 trophic levels is the most advantageous.

This is option (A) 2 trophic levels.

rows.stem:
Consider the following statements about ozone :

(a) Ozone is poisonous gas.

(b) Ozone shields the earth’s surface from the infrared radiation from the sun.

(c) Ozone is a product of UV radiations acting on oxygen molecule.

(d) At the lower level of the earth’s atmosphere, ozone performs most essential function.

The correct statements are
rows.solution:
Statement (a) is true: ozone is a deadly poisonous gas. Statement (b) is false: ozone shields the earth from ultraviolet radiation, not infrared. Statement (c) is true: ozone forms when UV radiation splits oxygen molecules into free atoms, which combine with \(\mathrm{O_2}\) to form \(\mathrm{O_3}\). Statement (d) is false: ozone does its essential job of absorbing UV radiation in the higher levels of the atmosphere.

So statements (a) and (c) are correct, which is option (B).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** A piece of Zinc metal gets reddish brown coating when kept in copper sulphate solution for some time.

**Reason (R) :** Copper is more reactive metal than Zinc.
rows.context: Q. Nos. 17 to 20 consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R), answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution:
Zinc is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper sulphate solution, and the reddish brown copper deposits on the zinc:

\(\mathrm{Zn(s) + CuSO_4(aq) \rightarrow ZnSO_4(aq) + Cu(s)}\)

So the Assertion is true. The Reason says copper is more reactive than zinc, which is the opposite of the truth, so the Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Offsprings produced by asexual reproduction are genetically similar to the parents.

**Reason (R) :** Asexual reproduction involves a single parent.
rows.context: Q. Nos. 17 to 20 consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R), answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution:
Asexual reproduction involves only one parent and no fusion of gametes, so the DNA of the offspring is copied from that single parent. The offspring are therefore genetically similar to the parent (apart from small variations from copying errors).

The Reason is true and explains the Assertion. This is option (A).

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Red light signals are used to stop the vehicles on the road.

**Reason (R) :** Red coloured light is scattered the most so as to be visible from a large distance.
rows.context: Q. Nos. 17 to 20 consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R), answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution:
Red light is used for stop signals on the road, so the Assertion is true. Red light has the longest wavelength and is scattered the LEAST by fog or smoke, so it can be seen from a large distance. The Reason says it is scattered the most, so the Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The waste we generate daily may be biodegradable or non-biodegradable.

**Reason (R) :** The waste generated, if not disposed off properly may cause serious environmental problems.
rows.context: Q. Nos. 17 to 20 consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R), answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution:
Waste is either biodegradable (broken down by microorganisms) or non-biodegradable, so the Assertion is true. Waste that is not disposed of properly does cause serious environmental problems, so the Reason is also true. But the Reason does not explain why waste falls into these two kinds.

Both are true and the Reason is not the correct explanation, which is option (B).

rows.stem: When magnesium ribbon is burnt in air, an ash of white colour is produced. Write chemical equation for the reaction giving the chemical name of the ash produced. State the type of chemical reaction giving justification for your answer.
rows.solution:
\(\mathrm{2Mg(s) + O_2(g) \rightarrow 2MgO(s)}\)

The white ash is magnesium oxide.

It is a combination reaction, because two substances (magnesium and oxygen) combine to form a single product (magnesium oxide).

rows.stem: Where are auxins synthesized ? How do they promote phototropism ?
rows.solution:
Auxins are synthesised at the shoot tip.

When light falls on one side of the plant, auxin diffuses towards the shady side of the shoot. The higher concentration of auxin makes the cells on the side away from the light grow longer, so the shoot bends towards the light. This is phototropism.

rows.stem: List any two pairs of visible contrasting characters of garden pea plants used by Mendel for his experiments stating the dominant and recessive characters in each pair.
rows.solution:
Any two pairs:

1. Tall plant (dominant) and dwarf plant (recessive).

2. Yellow seeds (dominant) and green seeds (recessive).

3. Round seeds (dominant) and wrinkled seeds (recessive).

4. Violet flowers (dominant) and white flowers (recessive).

rows.stem: In human beings, the probability of getting a male or a female child is 50%. Explain with the help of a flow diagram only.
rows.solution:
Parents: father XY \(\times\) mother XX

Gametes: the father makes two kinds of sperm, X and Y, in equal numbers; the mother makes only X eggs.

Fertilisation:

egg X + sperm X \(\rightarrow\) XX (female child)

egg X + sperm Y \(\rightarrow\) XY (male child)

Since the X and Y sperms are equal in number and either may fertilise the egg, half the children are XX (girls, 50%) and half are XY (boys, 50%). The sex of the child is decided by the chromosome the father contributes.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem: When do we say that a particular person is suffering from hypermetropia ? List two causes of this defect. Name the type of lens used to correct this defect.
rows.solution:
A person suffers from hypermetropia (far-sightedness) when he can see distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects distinctly.

Causes: (i) the focal length of the eye lens is too long; (ii) the eyeball has become too small.

It is corrected with a convex (converging) lens of suitable power.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem: Draw a labelled diagram to show the pattern of magnetic field lines produced due to a current carrying straight conductor. Mark on it the direction of current in the conductor and the direction of magnetic field lines.
rows.solution:
Diagram: a straight wire passes vertically through a horizontal sheet of cardboard and is connected through a variable resistance, an ammeter, a key and a battery. On the cardboard, draw concentric circles centred on the wire; these are the magnetic field lines.

Mark an arrow on the wire for the current and arrows on the circles for the field. By the right-hand thumb rule, if the current flows upward, the field lines go anticlockwise when seen from above (they reverse if the current is reversed).

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem: Name the device used to magnetise a piece of magnetic material. Draw a labelled diagram to show the arrangement used for the magnetisation of a cylinder made of soft iron.
rows.solution:
A current-carrying solenoid is used (it makes the iron an electromagnet). The marking scheme also accepts a permanent magnet.

Diagram: draw a solenoid (a coil of many turns of insulated copper wire) with the soft iron cylinder placed inside it. Connect the ends of the coil to a battery and a key. Label the current-carrying solenoid and the soft iron rod. When the key is closed, the strong magnetic field inside the solenoid magnetises the soft iron rod.

rows.stem: What are decomposers ? List two consequences of their absence in an ecosystem.
rows.solution:
Decomposers are microorganisms, such as bacteria and fungi, that break down the complex organic substances in dead plants and animals and their wastes into simple inorganic substances.

Consequences of their absence (any two): dead plants and animals would pile up in the environment; the nutrients would not be recycled, so the soil would not be replenished; the rotting matter would give a foul smell and flies would breed.

rows.stem:
State reasons for the following :

(a) Zinc oxide is an amphoteric oxide.

(b) Sodium metal is stored in bottle filled with kerosene oil.

(c) In the reactions of nitric acid with metals, generally hydrogen gas is not evolved.
rows.solution:
(a) Zinc oxide reacts with both acids and bases to give a salt and water, so it is amphoteric:

\(\mathrm{ZnO + 2HCl \rightarrow ZnCl_2 + H_2O}\)

\(\mathrm{ZnO + 2NaOH \rightarrow Na_2ZnO_2 + H_2O}\) (sodium zincate)

(b) Sodium reacts so vigorously with the oxygen (and moisture) of air that it catches fire if kept in the open. Kerosene keeps it out of contact with air, which prevents accidental fires.

(c) Nitric acid is a strong oxidising agent. It oxidises the hydrogen produced to water and is itself reduced to oxides of nitrogen, so hydrogen gas is not evolved. (Magnesium and manganese do give hydrogen with very dilute nitric acid.)

rows.stem:
State giving reason the reduction process to obtain the following metals from their compounds :

(i) Mercury,

(ii) Copper and

(iii) Sodium
rows.solution:
(i) Mercury: it is low in the reactivity series, so it is obtained by heating alone. Its ore, cinnabar (HgS), is heated in air (roasted) to mercuric oxide, which on further heating is reduced to mercury:

\(\mathrm{2HgS(s) + 3O_2(g) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2HgO(s) + 2SO_2(g)}\)

\(\mathrm{2HgO(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2Hg(l) + O_2(g)}\)

(ii) Copper: it is also low in reactivity, so it too is obtained by heating alone. Its sulphide ore, \(\mathrm{Cu_2S}\), is roasted in air, and the copper(I) oxide formed reacts with the remaining sulphide to give copper:

\(\mathrm{2Cu_2S + 3O_2(g) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2Cu_2O(s) + 2SO_2(g)}\)

\(\mathrm{2Cu_2O + Cu_2S \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 6Cu(s) + SO_2(g)}\)

(iii) Sodium: it is very high in the reactivity series and has more affinity for oxygen than carbon has, so it cannot be obtained by reducing its compounds with carbon. It is obtained by electrolytic reduction of molten sodium chloride; sodium is deposited at the cathode and chlorine is set free at the anode:

\(\mathrm{Na^+ + e^- \rightarrow Na}\)

rows.stem:
State giving reason for the change in appearance observed when each of the following metal is exposed to atmospheric air for some time :

(i) Silver,

(ii) Copper and

(iii) Iron
rows.solution:
(i) Silver: the shiny silver-white surface turns black. Silver reacts with sulphur compounds in the air to form a black coating of silver sulphide, \(\mathrm{Ag_2S}\).

(ii) Copper: the shiny reddish brown surface gets a green coating. Copper reacts with moist carbon dioxide in the air to form green basic copper carbonate, \(\mathrm{CuCO_3 \cdot Cu(OH)_2}\).

(iii) Iron: the grey surface gets a reddish brown flaky coating. Iron reacts with oxygen and moisture in the air to form rust (hydrated iron(III) oxide).

rows.stem: We water the soil but it reaches the topmost leaves of the plants. Explain in brief the process involved.
rows.solution:
The roots absorb water from the soil, and the xylem vessels and tracheids of the roots, stems and leaves are interconnected, forming a continuous system of water-conducting channels up to the leaves.

At the leaves, water evaporates through the stomata (transpiration). The loss of this water creates a suction (the transpiration pull), which pulls water up through the xylem from the roots to the topmost leaves.

(At night, when the stomata are closed, root pressure also helps push water up the xylem.)

rows.subtopic: Human Brain and Protection of Nervous Tissue
rows.stem:
(a) List two constituents of Central Nervous System (CNS). How are these components protected from injuries ?

(b) Write two limitations of the use of electrical impulses.
rows.solution:
(a) The central nervous system consists of the brain and the spinal cord.

The brain is protected inside a bony box, the skull (cranium), where it sits in a fluid-filled balloon that absorbs shocks. The spinal cord is protected by the vertebral column (backbone).

(b) Limitations of electrical impulses:

1. They reach only those cells that are connected by nervous tissue, not each and every cell in the body.

2. Once a cell has generated and transmitted an impulse, it takes some time to reset before it can generate a new one, so cells cannot generate impulses continuously.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: Name and explain the phenomenon of light due to which the path of a beam of light becomes visible when it enters a smoke filled room through a small hole. Also state the dependence of colour of the light we receive on the size of the particle of the medium through which the beam of light passes.
rows.solution:
The phenomenon is the scattering of light (the Tyndall effect).

The smoke contains very fine particles. When the beam of light strikes these particles, the light is scattered (reflected diffusely) in all directions, and the scattered light reaching our eyes makes the path of the beam visible.

The colour of the scattered light depends on the size of the particles: very fine particles scatter mainly blue light (shorter wavelengths), while larger particles scatter light of longer wavelengths. If the particles are large enough, the scattered light may even appear white.

rows.stem: Explain in brief the function of an electric fuse in a domestic circuit. An electric heater of current rating 3 kW; 220 V is to be operated in an electric circuit of rating 5 A. What is likely to happen when the heater is switched **‘ON’** ? Justify your answer with necessary calculation.
rows.solution:
An electric fuse is a wire of low melting point connected in series with the circuit. If the current exceeds the safe limit (because of overloading or a short circuit), the fuse wire heats up, melts and breaks the circuit, preventing damage to the appliances and the circuit.

For the heater, \(P = 3\) kW \(= 3000\) W and \(V = 220\) V. From \(P = VI\),

\(I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{3000}{220} \approx 13{\cdot}6\) A.

This is far more than the 5 A rating of the circuit, so when the heater is switched on the fuse wire will melt and break the circuit (the heater cannot be run safely on this circuit).

rows.stem:
(a) State Ohm’s law. Write formula for the equivalent resistance \(R_p\) of the parallel combination of three resistors of values \(R_1\), \(R_2\) and \(R_3\).

(b) Find the resistance of the following network of resistors :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - (b) the network is given only as a drawing: three resistors, each labelled R, between terminals X and Y; how they are connected (which in series, which in parallel) is what (b) tests and is withheld here. Page idx 20.
rows.solution:
(a) Ohm's law: the potential difference \(V\) across the ends of a given metallic wire in an electric circuit is directly proportional to the current \(I\) flowing through it, provided its temperature remains the same, so \(V = IR\).

For three resistors in parallel: \(\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{R_1} + \dfrac{1}{R_2} + \dfrac{1}{R_3}\).

(b) In the network one resistor \(R\) is in series with a pair of resistors \(R\) connected in parallel.

The parallel pair: \(\dfrac{1}{R'} = \dfrac{1}{R} + \dfrac{1}{R} = \dfrac{2}{R}\), so \(R' = \dfrac{R}{2}\).

Adding the series resistor: \(R + \dfrac{R}{2} = \dfrac{3R}{2}\).

The resistance between X and Y is \(\dfrac{3R}{2}\).

rows.stem:
(i) Five solutions A, B, C, D and E when tested with pH paper showed pH as 4, 1, 13, 7 and 10 respectively. Which solution is :

(1) Strongly acidic (2) Strongly alkaline (3) Weakly acidic (4) Neutral and (5) Weakly alkaline ? Arrange the solutions in increasing order of \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ion concentration.

(ii) Write the name and formula of (1) an acidic salt and (2) a basic salt giving the name of the parent acid and parent base used to form the salt in each case.
rows.solution:
(i) The lower the pH, the more acidic the solution; pH 7 is neutral and above 7 is alkaline.

(1) Strongly acidic: solution B (pH 1).

(2) Strongly alkaline: solution C (pH 13).

(3) Weakly acidic: solution A (pH 4).

(4) Neutral: solution D (pH 7).

(5) Weakly alkaline: solution E (pH 10).

The \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ion concentration rises as the pH falls, so in increasing order: \(\mathrm{C < E < D < A < B}\).

(ii) (1) Acidic salt: ammonium chloride, \(\mathrm{NH_4Cl}\). Parent acid: hydrochloric acid, HCl (strong). Parent base: ammonium hydroxide, \(\mathrm{NH_4OH}\) (weak).

(2) Basic salt: sodium carbonate, \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}\). Parent acid: carbonic acid, \(\mathrm{H_2CO_3}\) (weak). Parent base: sodium hydroxide, NaOH (strong).

(Any other correct salt of a strong acid and a weak base, or of a weak acid and a strong base, is equally acceptable.)

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem: Name and state in brief the process which is used to prepare sodium hydroxide from sodium chloride. In this process along with the main product two gases ‘X’ and ‘Y’ are also given off at the two electrodes. Name ‘X’ and ‘Y’ specifying the name of their respective electrode at which each gas is obtained. One of these gases when reacts with dry calcium hydroxide produces a compound ‘Z’ which is widely used in water treatment plants and textile industries. Name Z and write chemical equation for the reaction involved in its formation.
rows.solution:
The process is the chlor-alkali process. When electricity is passed through an aqueous solution of sodium chloride (brine), it decomposes to form sodium hydroxide:

\(\mathrm{2NaCl(aq) + 2H_2O(l) \rightarrow 2NaOH(aq) + Cl_2(g) + H_2(g)}\)

X is chlorine gas, given off at the anode. Y is hydrogen gas, given off at the cathode. Sodium hydroxide solution forms near the cathode. (It is called chlor-alkali after its products: chlorine and an alkali.)

Chlorine reacts with dry slaked lime to give Z, bleaching powder (\(\mathrm{CaOCl_2}\)):

\(\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2 + Cl_2 \rightarrow CaOCl_2 + H_2O}\)

rows.stem:
(i) What are spores ? On which structures are they formed ? How do they overcome unfavourable conditions ? Name the organism which multiplies with the help of these structures.

(ii) Give two reasons why some plants are grown by the method of vegetative propagation. List two methods used to grow plants vegetatively.
rows.solution:
(i) Spores are tiny reproductive structures that detach from the parent and, on reaching a suitable surface, grow into new individuals.

They are formed in sac-like structures called sporangia (singular, sporangium), at the tips of thread-like hyphae.

Spores are covered by thick walls that protect them until they come in contact with a moist surface and can begin to grow.

Rhizopus (bread mould) multiplies by spores.

(ii) Reasons (any two): it is used for plants that have lost the capacity to produce seeds (such as banana, orange, rose and jasmine); plants raised this way bear flowers and fruits earlier than plants grown from seeds; all the new plants are genetically similar to the parent, so its desirable characters are kept.

Methods (any two): layering, grafting, cutting.

rows.stem:
(i) Study the diagram given below and name the parts marked as A, B and C. What happens when B reaches C in the ovary ? Mention its significance.

(ii) Write the post fertilisation changes that occur in a flower.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - (i) asks to name the parts marked A, B and C on a drawn longitudinal section of a pistil with three labelled pointers; the labels exist only in the drawing and their identities (the answer) are withheld here. Page idx 24.
rows.solution:
(i) A is the male germ cell (male gamete), B is the pollen tube and C is the female germ cell (female gamete, the egg) in the ovule.

After pollination the pollen tube grows out of the pollen grain and travels through the style to reach the ovule in the ovary. When it reaches the ovule, the male germ cell it carries fuses with the female germ cell. This is fertilisation, and it forms a zygote.

Significance: the zygote is capable of growing into a new plant; it divides to form the embryo in the seed.

(ii) After fertilisation:

1. The zygote divides several times to form an embryo within the ovule.

2. The ovule develops a tough coat and is converted into a seed.

3. The ovary grows rapidly and ripens to form the fruit.

4. The petals, sepals, stamens, style and stigma may shrivel and fall off.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem:
(i) Draw a ray diagram to show the path of the refracted ray in each of the following cases :

A ray of light incident on a concave lens

(1) parallel to its principal axis, and

(2) is directed towards its principal focus.

(ii) A 4 cm tall object is placed perpendicular to the principal axis of convex lens of focal length 24 cm. The distance of object from the lens is 16 cm. Find the position and size of image formed.
rows.solution:
(i) (1) A ray parallel to the principal axis, after refraction through a concave lens, diverges and appears to come from the principal focus \(\mathrm{F_1}\) on the same side of the lens as the object. Draw the incident ray parallel to the axis, the refracted ray bending away from the axis, and a dotted line from the refracted ray back to \(\mathrm{F_1}\).

(2) A ray directed towards the principal focus \(\mathrm{F_2}\) on the other side of the lens emerges parallel to the principal axis after refraction. Draw the incident ray heading towards \(\mathrm{F_2}\), with its continuation dotted, and the refracted ray leaving parallel to the axis.

Mark the directions of the rays with arrows.

(ii) For a convex lens, \(u = -16\) cm, \(f = +24\) cm and \(h = 4\) cm. By the lens formula \(\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\),

\(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{24} - \dfrac{1}{16} = \dfrac{2 - 3}{48} = -\dfrac{1}{48}\), so \(v = -48\) cm.

The image is 48 cm from the lens on the same side as the object.

\(m = \dfrac{h'}{h} = \dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{-48}{-16} = 3\), so \(h' = 3 \times 4 = 12\) cm.

The image is 12 cm tall, virtual, erect and enlarged.

rows.stem:
(i) Draw a ray diagram to show the path of the reflected ray in each of the following cases :

A ray of light incident on a convex mirror

(1) parallel to its principal axis, and

(2) is directed towards its principal focus

(ii) A 1.5 cm tall candle flame is placed perpendicular to the principal axis of a concave mirror of focal length 12 cm. If the distance of the flame from the pole of the mirror is 18 cm, use mirror formula to determine the position and size of the image formed.
rows.solution:
(i) (1) A ray parallel to the principal axis, after reflection from a convex mirror, appears to diverge from the principal focus F behind the mirror. Draw the incident ray parallel to the axis, the reflected ray going back away from the axis, and a dotted line from the point of incidence to F behind the mirror.

(2) A ray directed towards the principal focus F behind a convex mirror is reflected parallel to the principal axis. Draw the incident ray heading towards F (continued dotted behind the mirror) and the reflected ray going back parallel to the axis.

Mark the directions of the rays with arrows.

(ii) For a concave mirror, \(f = -12\) cm, \(u = -18\) cm and \(h = 1{\cdot}5\) cm. By the mirror formula \(\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\),

\(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = -\dfrac{1}{12} + \dfrac{1}{18} = \dfrac{-3 + 2}{36} = -\dfrac{1}{36}\), so \(v = -36\) cm.

The image is 36 cm in front of the mirror.

\(m = \dfrac{h'}{h} = -\dfrac{v}{u} = -\dfrac{-36}{-18} = -2\), so \(h' = -2 \times 1{\cdot}5 = -3{\cdot}0\) cm.

The image is 3.0 cm tall, real, inverted and enlarged.

rows.stem: Write the molecular formula of first two members of homologous series having functional group \(\mathrm{{-}Br}\).
rows.context: More than three million carbon compounds have been discovered in the field of chemistry. The diversity of these compounds is due to the capacity of carbon atoms for bonding with one another as well as with other atoms. Most of the carbon compounds are poor conductors of electricity and have low melting and boiling points.
rows.solution: The homologous series with the functional group \(\mathrm{{-}Br}\) is the bromoalkanes. The first two members are \(\mathrm{CH_3Br}\) (bromomethane) and \(\mathrm{C_2H_5Br}\) (bromoethane).

rows.stem:
Given below are the formulae of some functional groups :

(i) \(\mathrm{{-}CHO}\), (ii) \(\mathrm{{-}CO{-}}\)

Write the name of these functional groups.
rows.context: More than three million carbon compounds have been discovered in the field of chemistry. The diversity of these compounds is due to the capacity of carbon atoms for bonding with one another as well as with other atoms. Most of the carbon compounds are poor conductors of electricity and have low melting and boiling points.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the two functional groups are printed as structural formulas, (i) a carbon with one free valence bonded to H and double-bonded to O, (ii) a carbon with two free valences double-bonded to O; the stem carries their condensed formulas, which are the same groups. Page idx 26.
rows.solution:
(i) \(\mathrm{{-}CHO}\) is the aldehyde group.

(ii) \(\mathrm{{-}CO{-}}\) is the ketone group.

rows.stem: What would be observed on adding a 5% alkaline potassium permanganate drop by drop to some warm ethanol taken in a test tube ? State the role of \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) in the reaction and write the chemical equation for the reaction involved.
rows.context: More than three million carbon compounds have been discovered in the field of chemistry. The diversity of these compounds is due to the capacity of carbon atoms for bonding with one another as well as with other atoms. Most of the carbon compounds are poor conductors of electricity and have low melting and boiling points.
rows.solution:
The purple colour of the potassium permanganate disappears as each drop is added, because it is used up in oxidising the ethanol. (Once all the ethanol is oxidised, the colour of further drops no longer disappears.)

\(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) acts as an oxidising agent: it adds oxygen to ethanol and converts it to ethanoic acid.

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{alkaline } KMnO_4,\ \text{heat}} CH_3COOH}\)

rows.stem: Write the name of the compound formed when ethanol is heated at 443 K temperature with excess of conc. \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\). What is the role of conc. \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) in the reaction ? Write the chemical equation for the reaction involved.
rows.context: More than three million carbon compounds have been discovered in the field of chemistry. The diversity of these compounds is due to the capacity of carbon atoms for bonding with one another as well as with other atoms. Most of the carbon compounds are poor conductors of electricity and have low melting and boiling points.
rows.solution:
The compound formed is ethene.

Concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent: it removes water from ethanol.

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{hot conc. } H_2SO_4,\ 443\ K} CH_2{=}CH_2 + H_2O}\)

rows.stem: Name the glands present in the buccal cavity and write the components of food on which the secretion of these glands act upon.
rows.context: Human digestive system is a tube running from mouth to anus. Its main function is to breakdown complex molecules present in the food which cannot be absorbed as such into smaller molecules. These molecules are absorbed across the walls of the tube and the absorbed food reaches each and every cell of the body where it is utilised for obtaining energy.
rows.solution: The salivary glands. Their secretion, saliva, contains the enzyme salivary amylase, which acts on starch (carbohydrate) and breaks it down to sugar.

rows.stem: Two organs have a sphincter muscle at their exit. Name them.
rows.context: Human digestive system is a tube running from mouth to anus. Its main function is to breakdown complex molecules present in the food which cannot be absorbed as such into smaller molecules. These molecules are absorbed across the walls of the tube and the absorbed food reaches each and every cell of the body where it is utilised for obtaining energy.
rows.solution: The stomach (its exit into the small intestine is regulated by a sphincter muscle) and the anus (the exit of waste is regulated by the anal sphincter).

rows.stem:
What will happen if :

(i) mucus is not secreted by the gastric glands.

(ii) Villi are absent in the small intestine.
rows.context: Human digestive system is a tube running from mouth to anus. Its main function is to breakdown complex molecules present in the food which cannot be absorbed as such into smaller molecules. These molecules are absorbed across the walls of the tube and the absorbed food reaches each and every cell of the body where it is utilised for obtaining energy.
rows.solution:
(i) Mucus protects the inner lining of the stomach from the action of the hydrochloric acid. Without it, the acid would damage the stomach lining, causing ulcers.

(ii) The villi greatly increase the surface area for absorption of digested food in the small intestine. Without them the absorption area would be much smaller, so the digested food would not be absorbed properly.

rows.stem: “Bile juice does not contain any enzyme, yet it has important roles in digestion.” Justify the statement.
rows.context: Human digestive system is a tube running from mouth to anus. Its main function is to breakdown complex molecules present in the food which cannot be absorbed as such into smaller molecules. These molecules are absorbed across the walls of the tube and the absorbed food reaches each and every cell of the body where it is utilised for obtaining energy.
rows.solution:
Bile has no enzyme but plays two important roles:

1. Emulsification of fats: bile salts break the large fat globules into smaller ones, increasing their surface area so that lipase can act on them efficiently.

2. The food coming from the stomach is acidic; bile makes it alkaline so that the pancreatic enzymes can act.

rows.stem:
State what happens when

(i) key \(\mathrm{K_1}\) is closed.

(ii) key \(\mathrm{K_2}\) is closed.
rows.context: In a domestic circuit five LED bulbs are arranged as shown. The source voltage is 220 V and the power rating of each bulb is marked in the circuit diagram. Based on the following circuit diagram, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit (a battery, an ammeter, keys \(\mathrm{K_1}\) and \(\mathrm{K_2}\), bulb A rated 22 W, 220 V and bulbs B, C, D and E each rated 11 W; 55 V) is given only as a drawing; how the bulbs are connected and which key controls which bulbs is what the sub-parts test and is withheld here. Page idx 28.
rows.solution:
(i) When key \(\mathrm{K_1}\) is closed, only bulb A glows. It is connected directly across the 220 V source.

(ii) When key \(\mathrm{K_2}\) is closed, bulbs B, C, D and E glow. They are connected in series across the 220 V source, so each gets 55 V.

rows.stem: Find the current drawn by the bulb B when it glows.
rows.context: In a domestic circuit five LED bulbs are arranged as shown. The source voltage is 220 V and the power rating of each bulb is marked in the circuit diagram. Based on the following circuit diagram, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit (a battery, an ammeter, keys \(\mathrm{K_1}\) and \(\mathrm{K_2}\), bulb A rated 22 W, 220 V and bulbs B, C, D and E each rated 11 W; 55 V) is given only as a drawing, and bulb B's rating is marked only there; the connections are withheld here. Page idx 28.
rows.solution:
Bulb B is in series with three identical bulbs across 220 V, so it gets \(\dfrac{220}{4} = 55\) V, its rated voltage, and works at its rated power of 11 W.

From \(P = VI\): \(11 = 55 \times I\), so \(I = \dfrac{11}{55} = 0{\cdot}2\) A.

rows.stem:
Calculate

(i) the resistance of bulb B, and

(ii) total resistance of the combination of four bulbs B, C, D and E.
rows.context: In a domestic circuit five LED bulbs are arranged as shown. The source voltage is 220 V and the power rating of each bulb is marked in the circuit diagram. Based on the following circuit diagram, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit (a battery, an ammeter, keys \(\mathrm{K_1}\) and \(\mathrm{K_2}\), bulb A rated 22 W, 220 V and bulbs B, C, D and E each rated 11 W; 55 V) is given only as a drawing; how B, C, D and E are combined is what (ii) tests and is withheld here. Page idx 28.
rows.solution:
(i) \(R = \dfrac{V}{I} = \dfrac{55}{0{\cdot}2} = 275\,\Omega\). (Equally, \(R = \dfrac{V^2}{P} = \dfrac{55^2}{11} = 275\,\Omega\).)

(ii) The four bulbs B, C, D and E are in series, so the total resistance is \(4 \times 275 = 1100\,\Omega\).

rows.stem: What would happen to the glow of all the bulbs in the circuit when keys \(\mathrm{K_1}\) and \(\mathrm{K_2}\) both are closed and the bulb C suddenly get fused ? Give reason to justify your answer.
rows.context: In a domestic circuit five LED bulbs are arranged as shown. The source voltage is 220 V and the power rating of each bulb is marked in the circuit diagram. Based on the following circuit diagram, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit (a battery, an ammeter, keys \(\mathrm{K_1}\) and \(\mathrm{K_2}\), bulb A rated 22 W, 220 V and bulbs B, C, D and E each rated 11 W; 55 V) is given only as a drawing; how the bulbs are connected is what this part tests and is withheld here. Page idx 28.
rows.solution:
Bulb A keeps glowing with the same brightness, while bulbs B, D and E stop glowing.

Reason: B, D and E are connected in series with C, so when C fuses their circuit is broken and no current flows through them. Bulb A is in a separate branch connected in parallel with this series combination, so it still gets the full 220 V and is unaffected.
